data-storage-converter.quickAnswer: 1 GB (decimal) = 1,000 MB, while 1 GiB (binary) = 1,024 MiB. Pick any from/to pair - for example, 8 gigabits ÷ 8 = 1 gigabyte, so a "100 Mbps" connection downloads at most 12.5 MB/s. Binary units (KiB, MiB, GiB, TiB) use powers of 1,024.
keyFacts: 8 bits = 1 byte. Divide bits by 8 to get bytes - the single most useful storage conversion.
Decimal units (KB, MB, GB, TB) multiply by 1,000 each step; binary units (KiB, MiB, GiB, TiB) multiply by 1,024.
Network speeds are sold in bits (Mbps); downloads are measured in bytes (MB/s) - divide by 8.
1 TB = 1,000 GB but 1 TiB = 1,024 GiB. The gap grows at each step: ~2.4% at kilo, ~7.4% at giga.
A single-layer DVD holds 4.7 GB; a dual-layer Blu-ray holds 50 GB.
Cloud storage is billed in decimal GB, which is why providers and operating systems report different numbers.
howTo: Choose the from-unit (bits, bytes, KB... up to TiB).
Read the instant result; swap reverses it.
data-storage-converter.formula:
result = value × (bytes per from-unit) ÷ (bytes per to-unit).
Bytes per unit: bit 0.125, B 1, KB 1,000, MB 1,000,000, GB 10⁹, TB 10¹², PB 10¹⁵, KiB 1,024, MiB 1,048,576, GiB 1,073,741,824, TiB 1,099,511,627,776.
Example: 1 GB → MB = 1 × 10⁹ ÷ 10⁶ = 1,000 MB.

faqs.q: How many MB are in 1 GB?
faqs.a: 1,000 MB in decimal (the storage-industry standard), or 1,024 MiB in binary. When someone says "GB" without specifying, storage makers mean 1,000 MB while operating systems usually mean 1,024 MiB.

faqs.q: How do I convert Mbps to MB/s?
faqs.a: Divide by 8. A 100 Mbps connection transfers at most 12.5 MB/s. In practice expect a bit less because of network overhead.

faqs.q: What is bigger: GB or GiB?
faqs.a: GiB is bigger. 1 GiB = 1,073,741,824 bytes while 1 GB = 1,000,000,000 bytes. The GiB is about 7.37% larger.

faqs.q: How many bits are in a byte?
faqs.a: 8 bits = 1 byte, always. This is the fixed definition behind every bits↔bytes conversion.

faqs.q: Why do I need both KB and KiB?
faqs.a: Because the industry used "KB" for both 1,000 and 1,024 bytes for decades, causing real confusion (and lawsuits). KiB/MiB/GiB are the unambiguous binary names standardized by the IEC.

faqs.q: How much is 1 TB in GB?
faqs.a: 1,000 GB decimal, or about 931.3 GiB binary - which is why a "1 TB" drive shows roughly 931 GB in your operating system.
